basics.name: Tianyi Wang
basics.label: Undergraduate Researcher · Computational Biology
basics.summary: Fourth-year undergraduate at Peking University (B.S. Biological Sciences, second major in Economics), working on single-cell and spatial omics, computational biology, and AI agents for scientific analysis.

work.name: Newman Lab, Stanford University
work.position: Visiting Research Student (Advisor: Aaron M. Newman)
work.summary: Development and evaluation of a de-novo analysis method for spatial transcriptomic data.
highlights: Designed metrics and an evaluation pipeline for fair comparison of model performance: ability to recover biology in spatial data, plus scalability analysis of runtime, memory, and scaling.
Benchmarked against a baseline and 3 other published methods across 3 scenarios spanning large-scale data and self-designed synthetic data.
Selected and curated the datasets used to demonstrate the method's biological interpretation and cross-model validation.

work.name: Zemin Zhang Lab, Peking University
work.position: Undergraduate Researcher (Advisors: Zemin Zhang, Dongfang Wang)
work.summary: Cross-Tissue Single-Cell and Spatial Analysis of Sex and Hormone Effects in MASH.
highlights: Integrated and annotated ~2.5M single cells across 21 tissues in a 2×2×2 design crossing MASH, sex, and hormone status, building a cross-tissue reference toward a 5M single-cell mouse atlas.
Resolved myeloid, B cell, and neutrophil populations to subtype level; identified myeloid subpopulations and gene programs whose responses to diet and sex differ across tissues.
Designed a unified compositional and pseudobulk differential-expression framework applied across all 21 tissues to separate diet, sex, and hormone effects.
Led the spatial analysis across 65 Xenium sections and 8 tissues, relating gene-program scores to neighborhood composition and validating trends in single-cell modality.

work.name: Zemin Zhang Lab, Peking University
work.position: Undergraduate Researcher (Advisors: Zemin Zhang, Dongfang Wang)
work.summary: Xenium 5k Spatial Atlas of the Hepatocellular Carcinoma Microenvironment.
highlights: Constructed a spatial atlas of 650,931 cells across 57 Xenium sections from an HCC cohort on combination targeted–immunotherapy; annotated 20 cell types from a ResolVI model.
Performed compositional-difference and cell-abundance analysis within each anatomical region, revealing distinct immune-infiltration and parenchymal landscapes.
Correlated cell-type fractions and spatial patterns with clinical outcomes via Cox regression, identifying candidate biomarkers for targeted/immunotherapy combination outcome.

work.name: Pertura / PerturaBench
work.summary: An execution-grounded authority layer for LLM agents in Perturb-seq analysis.
highlights: Gated every scientific claim on verified execution, analysis scope, and upstream dependencies rather than on the agent's own account of what it did.
Designed PerturaBench: 20 dependency-aware tasks over three Perturb-seq datasets and a donor-aware supplement, scoring 120 turns across three agent conditions and two prespecified repeats.

Prespecified the primary analysis and froze evaluators and thresholds before unblinding; reported clustered bootstrap confidence intervals and a sensitivity cohort, including the contrast that did not reproduce.
Reached 83.3% primary scientific fidelity vs. 44.4% and 38.9% for baselines, and 82.5% claim-authority success with no loss of informativeness.
